# Wanjaaro – Complete Empirical Cognitive & Skill Games Knowledge Base

> Wanjaaro (https://wanjaaro.com) is an open client-side web gaming and cognitive benchmarking platform featuring 106 instant games across 12 distinct disciplines. All tests execute entirely within the client browser using HTML5 Canvas, Web Audio, and hardware-accelerated timestamping with sub-millisecond precision, zero network ping distortion, and private local high-score persistence via browser localStorage.

## Table of Contents
1. Platform Architecture & Timing Integrity
2. Standardized Empirical Benchmark Dataset (Norms & Percentiles)
3. Skill Categories Overview (12 Disciplines)
4. Comprehensive Game Catalog & Rules Repository (106 Games)

---

## 1. Platform Architecture & Timing Integrity

- **Client-Side Execution**: Every game runs 100% on the user device processor and GPU. No frames or game loops are streamed from cloud servers, eliminating network round-trip ping jitter (typically 30ms-120ms on cloud services).
- **High-Resolution Microsecond Timing**: Latency measurements utilize hardware-backed browser timestamps with sub-millisecond precision relative to `requestAnimationFrame` display refresh intervals.
- **Privacy & Data Storage**: High scores, reaction time percentiles, round counts, and daily puzzle streaks are stored exclusively in the user's browser `localStorage`. No account registration, email, or login credentials are required. Third-party advertising cookies may be served according to the site's Privacy Policy (https://wanjaaro.com/privacy/).
- **Dual-Input Responsive Calibrations**: Supports touch inputs for mobile/tablet displays alongside precision keyboard and mouse polling for desktop workstations.

---

## 2. Standardized Empirical Benchmark Dataset (Norms & Percentiles)

The following reference norms are derived from experimental cognitive literature and validated response distributions. All scores reflect local client-side execution without network lag.

| Discipline | Metric | 10th % (Low) | 25th % | 50th % (Median) | 75th % | 90th % | 99th % (Elite) | Reference Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Visual Reaction Time | Visual Latency (ms) | 340 ms | 280 ms | **245 ms** | 215 ms | 190 ms | **165 ms** | Human Benchmark aggregate data & Kosinski visual response standards |
| Chimp Memory Test | Instant Recall Capacity (digits) | 4 digits | 6 digits | **8 digits** | 9 digits | 11 digits | **13 digits** | Kyoto University Primate Research Institute (Inoue & Matsuzawa) |
| Precision Aim Acquisition | Target Acquisition Time (ms) | 680 ms | 560 ms | **470 ms** | 390 ms | 330 ms | **275 ms** | Fitts's Law human-computer motor interaction standards & esports aiming distributions |
| Speed Typist Drill | Net Typing Velocity (WPM) | 26 WPM | 38 WPM | **52 WPM** | 68 WPM | 88 WPM | **115 WPM** | International Touch Typing Standards & aggregate touch-typing velocity distributions |
| Schulte Grid 5x5 | 25-Digit Search Completion (seconds) | 58 seconds | 46 seconds | **36 seconds** | 28 seconds | 22 seconds | **17 seconds** | Schulte Grid psychiatric diagnostic norm table (Walter Schulte, 1955) |
| Stroop Color Interference | Incongruent Delay Cost (ms delay) | 240 ms delay | 180 ms delay | **135 ms delay** | 95 ms delay | 65 ms delay | **35 ms delay** | J. Ridley Stroop (1935) interference cost literature & psychological baseline norms |
| Speed Addition Blitz | 30-Second Equations Solved (solved) | 6 solved | 11 solved | **17 solved** | 24 solved | 31 solved | **42 solved** | Mental arithmetic speed distributions under timed stimulus protocols |
| Klondike Solitaire Classic | Winning Moves Count (moves) | 165 moves | 140 moves | **122 moves** | 104 moves | 89 moves | **76 moves** | Klondike 52-card combinatorial analysis & solver simulation averages |
| Master Sudoku 9x9 | Logical Solving Time (minutes) | 28 minutes | 20 minutes | **14 minutes** | 9.5 minutes | 6.8 minutes | **4.2 minutes** | Standardized 9x9 Sudoku deduction times without guessing aids |

## 4. Comprehensive Game Catalog & Rules Repository

Below is the exhaustive reference documentation for all 106 games on Wanjaaro.

### 1. Reaction Time Test

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction-time/
- **Category**: Reflex & Reaction (https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **ms** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Click or tap the screen the moment the red background turns solid green.
- **What It Measures**: This test measures your simple visual response latency in milliseconds. It tracks the time between when the screen color changes and when your input device registers your click.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Tap or click to arm the sensor. Wait patiently while the screen is red. As soon as it flashes green, tap as fast as humanly possible. Tapping too early incurs a false-start penalty.
- **Verified Benchmark**: Metric: Visual stimulus response latency | Population Average: 215ms – 250ms | Elite Tier (Top 1%): < 180ms | Source: Human Benchmark aggregate reaction dataset (2020) & Kosinski visual latency norms (2008)

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Rest your finger gently on the mouse button or touchscreen before the light turns green.
2. Fix your gaze directly on the center of the screen to catch the color shift immediately.
3. Avoid anticipating the color change, as clicking early counts as a false start.
4. Take three deep breaths before each trial to keep your forearm muscles relaxed.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is considered a normal reaction time on this test?**
  A: Most healthy adults score between 215 and 250 milliseconds using a desktop mouse or responsive touchscreen.
- **Q: Why does tapping too early reset the round?**
  A: False starts are penalized because true reaction time measures response to a stimulus, not random guessing.
- **Q: Does screen refresh rate affect my score?**
  A: Yes, displays running at 144Hz or higher update the visual frame faster than older 60Hz screens, reducing input display delay by roughly 10 milliseconds.

---

### 2. Speed Flash Reflex

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-speed-flash/
- **Category**: Reflex & Reaction (https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Tap instantly when a white beacon appears, but keep your hand still when a red decoy flashes.
- **What It Measures**: This game measures selective visual response speed and motor inhibition. It evaluates your ability to act quickly on target cues while restraining movement on false cues.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Beacons will appear intermittently. Tap instantly when the beacon is WHITE. If the beacon is RED, hold your fire! Scores are calculated from reaction time minus false-tap penalties.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Focus entirely on recognizing the white hue before allowing your finger to press down.
2. Keep your hand hovering half an inch above the screen to prevent accidental taps on red decoys.
3. Build a steady rhythm rather than trying to rush every flash.
4. Remember that a single false tap on red deducts more points than a slightly slower white tap.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: How is the final score calculated in Speed Flash Reflex?**
  A: Your score adds points for quick taps on white targets and subtracts a fixed penalty for every tap on a red decoy.
- **Q: What happens if I miss a white beacon completely?**
  A: Missing a white beacon breaks your scoring streak and gives zero points for that interval.
- **Q: Is it better to prioritize accuracy or speed?**
  A: Accuracy is more important because the penalty for clicking a red decoy heavily outweighs small speed bonuses.

---

### 3. Hex Whack Reflex

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-whack-hex/
- **Category**: Reflex & Reaction (https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Clear active glowing honeycomb cells across the grid before their timers run down.
- **What It Measures**: This game measures multi-point spatial targeting and rapid hand-eye coordination. It tests how quickly you can locate newly lit targets across a wide area and tap them accurately.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A cluster of honeycomb cells will randomly ignite. Click or tap each illuminated cell before its countdown expires. The game accelerates every 5 successful hits.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Keep your eyes loosely focused on the grid center so your peripheral vision catches outer lights.
2. Tap with whichever hand is closest to the active target if you are playing on a touchscreen.
3. Prioritize older glowing cells that are closest to expiring over newly lit ones.
4. Use short, light taps to reset your hand position quickly for the next target.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Does the honeycomb grid speed up over time?**
  A: Yes, the time window for active cells shrinks progressively after every five successful hits.
- **Q: Can multiple cells light up at the same time?**
  A: As your score climbs, two or more cells can ignite simultaneously, requiring fast sequential taps.
- **Q: What causes a game over in Hex Whack?**
  A: Allowing three active hexagons to fade completely without being tapped ends the game.

---

### 4. Dodge Vector

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-dodge-ball/
- **Category**: Reflex & Reaction (https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **sec** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Guide your spark continuously through an accelerating storm of blue kinetic particles without getting hit.
- **What It Measures**: This test measures continuous evasion control and spatial trajectory anticipation. It records how many seconds you can sustain collision-free movement under increasing hazard density.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Move your mouse cursor or drag your finger to pilot the golden spark. Avoid all converging blue energy particles. Survive as long as you can while velocity escalates.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Stay near the central area of the arena to leave yourself escape routes in all directions.
2. Make small, controlled movements rather than sweeping panicky strokes across the screen.
3. Avoid backing yourself into corners where converging particles can trap you.
4. Watch the trajectories of incoming particles several steps ahead rather than staring only at your own spark.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Do the hazard particles move in random directions?**
  A: Particles bounce off boundaries according to kinetic reflection angles and slowly increase in velocity.
- **Q: Is mouse control or touch control recommended for Dodge Vector?**
  A: Both work well, but a low-friction mouse on desktop provides precise micro-adjustments with zero hand occlusion.
- **Q: How is survival time measured?**
  A: Your score tracks exact elapsed time from your first movement until particle contact.

### 5. Sound Reflex Cue

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-audio-snap/
- **Category**: Reflex & Reaction (https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **ms** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Press your mouse or spacebar the exact millisecond you hear the acoustic bell chime.
- **What It Measures**: This test measures pure auditory response time. Because auditory processing bypasses visual color interpretation, it benchmarks sound-triggered motor reflexes.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Click Start to enter listening mode. Keep your finger poised over the button or spacebar. When the chime sounds, click immediately. Your score is your pure acoustic reaction time.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Close your eyes or look away from the screen to eliminate visual distraction while listening.
2. Use headphones rather than laptop speakers for the clearest and earliest sound detection.
3. Position your index finger resting directly on the key to eliminate physical travel distance.
4. Breathe steadily and do not tense up while waiting for the sound cue.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Why are auditory reaction times generally faster than visual ones?**
  A: Sound signals reach the inner ear and brainstem pathways slightly faster than light waves travel through retinal receptors.
- **Q: Can background room noise affect my score?**
  A: Yes, a noisy environment creates auditory clutter, so testing in a quiet room or with headphones yields the cleanest scores.
- **Q: What is an average audio reaction time?**
  A: Typical auditory reaction times range between 170ms and 210ms for healthy adults.

---

### 6. Chroma Snap

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-color-switch/
- **Category**: Reflex & Reaction (https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Tap the matching button the moment the displayed color swatch aligns with the central target hue.
- **What It Measures**: This game measures rapid color matching and decision-making under continuous cyclic changes. It benchmarks how quickly you verify color parity before executing a physical tap.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A color name and card cycle rapidly. When the color card matches the primary banner color, tap immediately! Match streaks grant score multipliers.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Focus on overall saturation differences rather than reading color names.
2. Keep a light tap pressure so you can commit immediately when colors match.
3. Do not guess ahead; wait for visual confirmation of identical hues.
4. Maintain streaks to unlock higher combo point multipliers.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: How fast do the colors alternate?**
  A: Colors cycle every 400 to 800 milliseconds, giving you a brief window to confirm a match.
- **Q: What happens if I tap when the colors do not match?**
  A: An incorrect tap resets your current multiplier streak and subtracts a small penalty.
- **Q: Are the colors calibrated for colorblind players?**
  A: The game uses high-contrast primary swatches with distinct lightness levels to aid visibility.

### 7. Stoplight Precision

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-quick-brake/
- **Category**: Reflex & Reaction (https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Stop the rapidly filling progress needle as close to 100% as possible without crossing into the red zone.
- **What It Measures**: This game measures temporal estimation and precision stopping control. It evaluates your timing when judging speed and decelerating an action right before an overflow limit.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Press or tap to start the gauge needle accelerating. Tap Stop before it exceeds the critical red threshold line. The closer to 100% without going over, the higher your score.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Observe the needle speed during the first 50% of the gauge to gauge acceleration rate.
2. Aim for the 94% to 98% sweet spot for top tier points.
3. Never hesitate once the needle passes 90%, as stopping late in the red zone awards zero points.
4. Keep your clicking finger poised with zero slack on the mouse switch.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Does the gauge charge at a fixed speed every round?**
  A: No, the needle velocity varies randomly each round to prevent rote rhythmic timing.
- **Q: What is the penalty for exceeding 100%?**
  A: Crossing 100% is considered an overshot brake and scores 0 points for that specific attempt.
- **Q: How many brake trials make up one complete session?**
  A: A standard session consists of 5 consecutive stopping trials, with your final score being the average accuracy.

---

### 8. Trigger Tap Sprint

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-trigger-finger/
- **Category**: Reflex & Reaction (https://wanjaaro.com/reflex-reaction/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Register as many clean, individual finger taps as possible within a strict 5-second sprint.
- **What It Measures**: This game measures single-digit motor firing rate and burst tapping endurance. It benchmarks raw repetitive muscular cycling over a short duration.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Target discs flash on screen for only 400 milliseconds. Tap or click them before they disappear. Missing 3 targets terminates your run.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Use the tip of your index finger rather than a flat finger pad for crisper tactile rebound.
2. Keep your wrist grounded on the desk or table to isolate finger movement and reduce arm fatigue.
3. Tense your forearm slightly to establish a rapid fluttering cadence.
4. Tap firmly enough to register each switch actuation without bottoming out heavily.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Does jitter-clicking or butterfly clicking work in Trigger Tap Sprint?**
  A: Yes, advanced gaming clicking techniques are detected and counted accurately by the input listener.
- **Q: What is a typical score for a 5-second sprint?**
  A: Most players achieve between 30 and 45 taps (6 to 9 taps per second), while competitive clickers exceed 55 taps.
- **Q: Can I use two alternating fingers on mobile?**
  A: Yes, multi-touch is supported on touchscreens so you can alternate index and middle fingers.

---

### 9. Precision Sniper

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/aim-sniper/
- **Category**: Aim & Precision (https://wanjaaro.com/aim-precision/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Acquire and eliminate shrinking target nodes across the arena before they collapse to zero radius.
- **What It Measures**: This trainer measures ballistic cursor flick accuracy and fine cursor deceleration. It benchmarks how quickly and accurately you reposition your crosshair onto variable-sized targets.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Click or tap moving bullseyes before they collapse to zero size. Hitting closer to the dead center yields maximum points (up to 100 per target). Complete 15 targets.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Lower your mouse DPI sensitivity if you notice your cursor overshooting past small targets.
2. Flick your wrist directly toward the target center, then decelerate into a micro-correction.
3. Target shrinking discs first before they expire to preserve your consecutive streak multiplier.
4. Keep your arm relaxed and glide your mouse across a consistent, clean mousepad surface.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Do targets shrink at the same rate throughout the drill?**
  A: Targets shrink faster as your consecutive score streak increases, demanding faster flick timing.
- **Q: What is the optimal mouse sensitivity for Precision Sniper?**
  A: A medium sensitivity where one comfortable wrist swipe covers approximately half your screen width offers the best balance.
- **Q: How does miss penalty affect the score?**
  A: Clicking empty arena space deducts accuracy percentage and resets your active combo streak.

---

### 10. Orbit Synchronizer

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/aim-orbit-tap/
- **Category**: Aim & Precision (https://wanjaaro.com/aim-precision/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium

- **How to Play & Rules**: A satellite revolves around a circular orbital track. Tap when the satellite is exactly inside the target ring. Each round narrows the alignment window and increases orbital speed.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:

### 19. Spatial Span Matrix

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/memory-spatial-span/
- **Category**: Memory & Recall (https://wanjaaro.com/memory-recall/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Memorize the positions of flashed numbers across the grid, then click their hidden locations in ascending order (1 to 9).
- **What It Measures**: This test measures working memory capacity under rapid visual masking. It evaluates how many simultaneous spatial coordinates you can encode in a fraction of a second.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A set of tiles will glow for 1.5 seconds. Once they turn blank, tap the exact tiles that were highlighted. The grid size and count increase as your level rises.
- **Verified Benchmark**: Metric: Instantaneous spatial sequence recall | Population Average: 7 – 9 numbers | Elite Tier (Top 1%): 9 numbers in 0.65s (Ayumu benchmark) | Source: Inoue & Matsuzawa (2007) Kyoto University Primate Research Institute working memory study

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Group numbers into geometric shapes like triangles or lines to memorize clusters at once.
2. Anchor your eyes on numbers 1, 2, and 3 first, as tapping these quickly gives you time to recall later positions.
3. Do not try to memorize all positions at once; trace an imaginary path from 1 through the highest number.
4. Breathe steadily and stay calm during the brief flash interval before cards mask into white blocks.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Why is this challenge named after the chimpanzee Ayumu?**
  A: At Kyoto University, a young chimpanzee named Ayumu routinely recalled all 9 masked numbers accurately in under 0.7 seconds, outperforming human university students.
- **Q: What is the average human score on the spatial span test?**
  A: Most adults consistently remember 7 to 9 numbers, aligning with standard working memory limits.
- **Q: Does the flash duration change as levels progress?**
  A: Yes, higher difficulty stages reduce display exposure time from 1000 milliseconds down to 300 milliseconds.

### 20. Digit Span Challenge

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/memory-number-span/
- **Category**: Memory & Recall (https://wanjaaro.com/memory-recall/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **streak** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Memorize an expanding string of random digits displayed one by one, then type them back accurately.
- **What It Measures**: This test measures forward auditory-verbal working memory span. It records the maximum length of an un-grouped numerical sequence you can hold and reproduce.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Numbers appear sequentially on screen. Once the sequence ends, type or tap the numbers in the identical sequence. Reaching 8+ digits places you in the top 5% of recall.
- **Verified Benchmark**: Metric: Forward digit sequence capacity | Population Average: 7 ± 2 digits | Elite Tier (Top 1%): 12+ digits | Source: Miller, G. A. (1956) 'The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two', Psychological Review

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Sub-vocalize digits in chunks of three (like phone numbers: 4-8-1, 9-2-5) rather than single digits.
2. Focus intensely on the final two digits, which fade the fastest from immediate recall.
3. Type your answer in a steady, unbroken rhythm once the prompt input field unlocks.
4. Avoid looking away from the screen while digits are flashing in sequence.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is the standard benchmark for human digit span?**
  A: In 1956, psychologist George Miller identified that human short-term memory typically holds 7 ± 2 items (5 to 9 digits).
- **Q: How fast do the digits flash on screen?**
  A: Each digit appears individually for 800 milliseconds followed by a 200 millisecond blank interval.
- **Q: What is the difference between forward and backward digit span?**
  A: Forward digit span tests raw capacity, while backward digit span requires active mental manipulation before typing.

2. Use keyboard shortcut keys for instant match reporting rather than clicking with a mouse.

  A: Points are awarded for correct hits and correct rejections, with deductions for misses and false alarms.
- **Q: Can the difficulty be adjusted to 2-Back or 3-Back?**
  A: Yes, after achieving an 85% accuracy rate on 1-Back, higher N-Back levels unlock in the settings menu.

### 25. Speed Wordsmith

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/typing-speed-words/
- **Category**: Typing & Words (https://wanjaaro.com/typing-words/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **wpm** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Type words accurately across a continuous 60-second typing sprint to achieve high words per minute.
- **What It Measures**: This test measures net typing speed (WPM) and keystroke accuracy. It benchmarks your bimanual keyboard fluency across common English vocabulary.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Type the highlighted word and press Spacebar to proceed to the next word. Inaccurate keystrokes highlight red. The test concludes after 60 seconds with full WPM and accuracy metrics.
- **Verified Benchmark**: Metric: Net words per minute (WPM) | Population Average: 40 – 55 WPM | Elite Tier (Top 1%): 100+ WPM | Source: International typing speed distribution statistics (99th percentile touch typists)

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Focus on error-free typing first; rhythm and speed naturally follow from high accuracy.
2. Read one or two words ahead of what your fingers are actively typing.
3. Keep your wrists elevated slightly above the desk to prevent dragging fatigue.
4. Use all ten fingers on their standard home-row positions rather than hunting and pecking.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: How is net words per minute (WPM) calculated?**
  A: One word is standardized as five keystrokes. Net WPM is calculated as (Gross Words - Uncorrected Errors) divided by elapsed minutes.
- **Q: What is considered a good typing speed for general users?**
  A: The average adult types between 40 and 55 WPM, while professional transcriptionists and programmers often reach 80 to 100+ WPM.
- **Q: Does the test penalize backspacing to correct typos?**
  A: You can backspace to fix errors before pressing space, but fixing mistakes consumes valuable sprint seconds.

  A: Yes, points scale exponentially: a 6-letter word awards four times more points than two 3-letter words.
- **Q: Can letters be reused more than once per word?**
  A: You can only use each letter tile as many times as it appears in the scrambled rack for that round.

### 28. Reverse Typist

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/typing-reverse-echo/
- **Category**: Typing & Words (https://wanjaaro.com/typing-words/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Read words displayed on screen and type their letters backward in exact reverse order.
- **What It Measures**: This drill measures mental spelling inversion and lexical manipulation. It challenges your ability to break apart a word and reverse its character order before typing.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A word appears on screen. Type its letters in reverse order from right to left as fast as possible. Tests your brain's ability to invert mental phonemes.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Read the word from right to left in your mind before striking the first key.
2. Spell out suffixes first (for example, typing "g-n-i" for words ending in "-ing").
3. Do not rush; one wrong letter ruins the reverse sequence and requires backspacing.
4. Whisper the reversed letter sounds to yourself to maintain character order.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is an example of Reverse Typist gameplay?**
  A: If the prompt shows "PLANET", you must immediately type "TENALP" followed by the Enter or Space key.
- **Q: Does word length increase on higher levels?**
  A: Rounds begin with 3-letter words and progressively advance to complex 8-letter vocabulary.
- **Q: How does Reverse Typist score performance?**
  A: Points are based on words correctly inverted per minute along with accuracy percentages.

### 35. Stroop Color Conflict

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/perception-stroop-test/
- **Category**: Perception & Vision (https://wanjaaro.com/perception-vision/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Select the color of the ink the word is printed in, completely ignoring what the written word says.
- **What It Measures**: This benchmark measures cognitive conflict resolution and selective attention. It records the millisecond reaction delay caused when the semantic meaning of a word clashes with its visual font color.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A color name appears (e.g. the word "BLUE" written in RED ink). Select the button that matches the INK COLOR (Red), not the word text! A premier test of cognitive conflict resolution.
- **Verified Benchmark**: Metric: Semantic color-word interference delay | Population Average: 120ms – 180ms delay | Elite Tier (Top 1%): < 60ms delay | Source: Stroop, J. R. (1935) 'Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions', Journal of Experimental Psychology

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Look at the physical font color and speak the color name in your mind before reading the letters.
2. Squint slightly if you find the written word distracting, which blurs the text while keeping the color obvious.
3. Use the keyboard colored shortcut buttons to bypass cursor travel time.
4. Stay consistent; hesitating on conflict words costs significant latency points.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is the classic Stroop effect?**
  A: Discovered by J. Ridley Stroop in 1935, it demonstrates that humans read words automatically, creating a noticeable delay when asked to report the ink color instead of the word itself.
- **Q: What is a typical interference delay on the Stroop test?**
  A: Most people experience an interference slowdown between 120ms and 180ms when ink color contradicts word meaning.
- **Q: Do congruent words appear during the test?**
  A: Yes, baseline congruent trials (e.g. the word "RED" printed in red ink) are mixed in to measure your baseline reading speed.

### 37. Ebbinghaus Size Match

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/perception-size-illusion/
- **Category**: Perception & Vision (https://wanjaaro.com/perception-vision/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **%** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Judge which of two central circles is physically larger despite distracting surrounding circle rings.
- **What It Measures**: This test measures susceptibility to contextual visual size illusions (Ebbinghaus and Ponzo effects). It evaluates your ability to perceive true dimensions independent of surrounding relative scale cues.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Optical illusions make circles surrounded by large rings appear smaller, and vice-versa. Drag the slider until both center circles are identical in true diameter, then press Submit.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Block out the surrounding outer circles mentally and compare only the inner boundaries.
2. Measure the inner circle diameter against a stationary finger or cursor edge if allowed in practice mode.
3. Remember that large surrounding circles make an inner disc appear artificially smaller than it truly is.
4. Trust measured geometry rather than immediate contextual impressions.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What causes the Ebbinghaus size illusion?**
  A: The human visual system naturally estimates object size relative to surrounding visual context rather than in absolute terms.
- **Q: Can the two central circles ever be exactly identical in size?**
  A: Yes, select trials feature identical circles to test whether you can recognize parity despite unequal surrounding rings.
- **Q: How does the game score optical illusion resistance?**
  A: Scores are calculated from your error percentage across 10 progressive illusion pairs with decreasing size disparities.

### 41. Lights Out Matrix

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/logic-lights-out/
- **Category**: Logic & Puzzles (https://wanjaaro.com/logic-puzzles/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **moves** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Toggle grid cells until every single light in the matrix is completely turned off.
- **What It Measures**: This puzzle measures binary state logic and modular matrix arithmetic. It tests your ability to plan orthogonal toggle cascades where clicking one light flips its four immediate neighbors.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Clicking any grid button toggles its state (on/off) and also toggles the cells directly above, below, left, and right. Solve the puzzle by extinguishing every single light in fewest moves.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Remember that clicking any cell twice cancels itself out; each light should be toggled at most once.
2. Work systematically from the top row downward, chasing lit cells to the bottom row.
3. Study bottom-row residue patterns to determine which top-row cells need adjustment to solve the grid.
4. Keep track of corner cells, as they affect only three neighboring lights rather than five.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Is every starting Lights Out board solvable?**
  A: All puzzle configurations generated on Wanjaaro are guaranteed mathematically solvable from their starting state.
- **Q: What is the "chasing lights" strategy?**
  A: Chasing lights involves toggling the cell directly underneath any illuminated light row by row until all lights reach the bottom row.
- **Q: How is performance rated in Lights Out Matrix?**
  A: Puzzles are scored based on the total number of moves taken compared to the mathematical minimum move count.

### 43. Tower of Hanoi

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/logic-tower-hanoi/
- **Category**: Logic & Puzzles (https://wanjaaro.com/logic-puzzles/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **moves** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Transfer the entire stack of graduated discs from the first peg to the third peg without ever placing a larger disc on a smaller one.
- **What It Measures**: This mathematical puzzle measures recursive problem-solving and hierarchical state planning. It tests your ability to decompose a large objective into nested sub-goals.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Click a peg to pick up its top disk, then click a destination peg. You may only move one disk at a time, and no disk may ever sit atop a smaller disk. Complete in minimum 7 moves for 3 disks.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. For an odd number of discs, make your very first move directly to the destination peg.
2. For an even number of discs, make your very first move to the middle auxiliary peg.
3. Alternate between moving the smallest disc and the only other legally movable disc.
4. The smallest disc should always circulate in one consistent direction across the three pegs.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is the minimum number of moves to solve Tower of Hanoi?**
  A: The theoretical minimum is 2^n - 1 moves, where n is the number of discs (e.g. 7 moves for 3 discs, 31 moves for 5 discs).
- **Q: Can you place a larger disc on top of a smaller disc?**
  A: No, placing a larger disc onto a smaller one is an illegal move and rejected by the game engine.
- **Q: How many discs can be selected in this version?**
  A: You can choose between 3 discs (beginner), 4 discs (intermediate), and 5 or 6 discs (advanced challenge).

---

### 44. Water Jug Riddle

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/logic-water-pour/
- **Category**: Logic & Puzzles (https://wanjaaro.com/logic-puzzles/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **moves** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Fill, empty, and pour water between two un-marked jugs to measure out an exact requested target volume.
- **What It Measures**: This classic riddle measures Euclidean state-space search and arithmetic transfer logic. It evaluates how you combine container capacities to reach an exact numerical difference.
- **How to Play & Rules**: You have a 3L jug, a 5L jug, and an endless water tap. Fill, empty, and pour water between jugs until you have measured the exact target quantity. Classic Die Hard riddle!

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Repeatedly fill the larger jug, pour into the smaller jug until full, and empty the smaller jug when full.
2. Observe the greatest common divisor between the two jug sizes to understand step progression.
3. Work forwards from empty containers or backwards from the target volume.
4. Keep track of how much remaining capacity is left in the destination jug before pouring.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Can you partially fill a jug by guessing?**
  A: No, jugs have no measurement marks. You can only fill a jug completely, empty it completely, or pour until the recipient is full.
- **Q: What is a famous example of this puzzle?**
  A: The 3-gallon and 5-gallon jug puzzle was famously featured in the film Die Hard with a Vengeance to measure exactly 4 gallons.
- **Q: How is efficiency scored in Water Jug Riddle?**
  A: Scores reflect the least total pour, fill, and empty actions needed to produce the target volume.

### 45. Binary Byte Switcher

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/logic-binary-flip/
- **Category**: Logic & Puzzles (https://wanjaaro.com/logic-puzzles/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Toggle individual bit switches (0 and 1) along the byte row to match the requested decimal integer target.
- **What It Measures**: This drill measures binary-to-decimal base conversion and powers-of-two mental arithmetic. It tests your fluency with binary place values (128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1).
- **How to Play & Rules**: A target decimal number between 0 and 255 is displayed. Click the binary bit toggles (0 or 1) to make the sum of active power-of-two bits equal the target as fast as possible.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Compare your target number to 128; if greater or equal, toggle the 128 bit on and subtract 128 from your running sum.
2. Continue down the powers of two (64, 32, 16, etc.), toggling bits that fit into your remaining balance.
3. Remember that odd decimal numbers always require the final 1-bit to be turned on.
4. Familiarize yourself with power-of-two additions to calculate 8-bit bytes rapidly.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is the maximum decimal number you can build with an 8-bit byte?**
  A: An 8-bit byte with all bits toggled to 1 equals 255 (128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1).
- **Q: Does the game support reverse mode (binary to decimal)?**
  A: Yes, an alternating mode displays active binary switches and asks you to enter the equivalent decimal sum.
- **Q: How much time do you get per conversion problem?**
  A: Sprint mode gives you 15 seconds per conversion, with speed bonuses for answers submitted under 5 seconds.

- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **moves** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Rotate pipe segments across the grid to establish an unbroken, leak-free conduit from source valve to drain exit.
- **What It Measures**: This puzzle measures network topology visualization and path continuity planning. It evaluates how you align rotational connections so flow travels without dead ends.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Tap any pipe segment to rotate it 90 degrees clockwise. Align all conduits so water can flow in an unbroken path from the green inlet valve to the gold outlet reservoir.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Start connecting from the fixed source valve and the fixed destination drain first.
2. Examine corner pipes along outer grid walls, as their orientations are strictly limited by boundaries.
3. Ensure every branch of T-junctions feeds into a valid connector rather than hitting a blank wall.
4. Double check all loop closures before turning the master water valve on.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What happens when water is released into the pipe network?**
  A: Water flows through all valid connected segments. If it reaches an open end, it leaks and docks points.
- **Q: Can there be unused pipe segments left over on the grid?**
  A: Some complex puzzle levels include decorative dead-end pipe tiles that do not need to connect to the main line.
- **Q: How do you rotate a pipe segment?**
  A: Click or tap any pipe tile to rotate it 90 degrees clockwise; double-click rotates 180 degrees.

- **How to Play & Rules**: Use arrow keys or directional buttons to walk the warehouse worker. Push crates forward onto the golden target pads. Remember: you can only push crates, never pull them!

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:

2. Avoid pushing two crates side-by-side against a flat wall, which locks both crates permanently.

4. Fill the furthest storage pads first so already-stored crates do not block remaining pathways.

### 48. Knight's Leap Puzzle

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/logic-knights-tour/
- **Category**: Logic & Puzzles (https://wanjaaro.com/logic-puzzles/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **streak** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Guide the chess knight to visit as many squares on the board as possible without landing on any square twice.
- **What It Measures**: This classic chess problem measures graph traversal and constraint satisfaction. It tests your application of Warnsdorff heuristic rules across L-shaped knight moves.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Click any valid L-shaped knight move (2 squares along one axis, 1 square perpendicular). Visit as many distinct chessboard squares as possible. Can you touch all 25 squares?

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Apply Warnsdorff rule: always move the knight to the square with the fewest remaining legal exits.
2. Tour outer board perimeter squares and corners early, as they are the hardest to reach later.
3. Avoid jumping toward the board center early, as central squares provide vital transit routes for the endgame.
4. Look two moves ahead to ensure your destination square does not leave your knight completely stranded.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is a full Knight Tour?**
  A: A full tour visits every single square on the board (e.g. all 64 squares on an 8x8 board) exactly once.
- **Q: How does the chess knight move?**
  A: The knight moves in an "L-shape": two squares in one cardinal direction followed by one square perpendicular.
- **Q: What grid sizes are available in Knight Leap Puzzle?**
  A: You can start on a smaller 5x5 board (25 squares) to learn the heuristic before graduating to a full 8x8 chessboard.

- **Objective**: Place three matching marks in a continuous horizontal, vertical, or diagonal row against an adaptive AI opponent.
- **What It Measures**: This game measures minimax adversarial planning and fork detection. It tests your ability to anticipate opponent responses and block fork opportunities.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Place your X on the 3x3 grid. Form three-in-a-row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. Choose between Medium AI or Master Minimax bot that calculates all game trees.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Take the center square on your first turn whenever it is available to maximize future winning lines.
2. If your opponent opens in the center, always play a corner square to prevent immediate traps.
3. Create "forks"—scenarios with two simultaneous winning lines that your opponent cannot block at once.
4. Watch opposing moves carefully to block two-in-a-row threats before making aggressive plays.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Can the Smart AI be beaten on impossible difficulty?**
  A: Under strict minimax play, standard Tic-Tac-Toe is a mathematically solved game where flawless play always results in a draw.

  A: Yes, you can toggle between casual mode (which makes occasional blunders) and master mode (which plays optimal minimax strategy).

- **What It Measures**: This game measures vertical gravity column planning and parity trap creation. It tests how you control central columns and avoid giving your opponent setup moves.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Tap any column to drop a disc. Discs fall to the lowest unoccupied space. The first player to connect four discs in a row (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) wins!

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Control the center column (column 4); central discs participate in the highest number of potential winning lines.
2. Never drop a disc directly beneath your opponent's potential fourth winning square unless forced to.
3. Build multiple overlapping threats on both horizontal and diagonal planes simultaneously.
4. Keep track of odd versus even column parity when playing as player one or player two.

- **Q: Who moves first in match play?**

### 51. Game of Nim

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/strategy-nim-matches/
- **Category**: Strategy & Tactics (https://wanjaaro.com/strategy-tactics/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **streak** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Remove matchsticks from any single heap on your turn to force your opponent into taking the final matchstick.
- **What It Measures**: This mathematical game measures binary digital sums (nim-sum XOR calculation) and end-game state control. It benchmarks your application of combinatorial game theory principles.
- **How to Play & Rules**: On your turn, remove 1, 2, or 3 matchsticks from the heap. In this "misère" variation, whoever takes the very last match loses the game. Play strategically to force a win.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Calculate the binary XOR sum of heap sizes; an even nim-sum (zero) represents a winning balanced position.
2. Always leave your opponent in a state with an XOR sum of zero at the end of your turn.
3. In the endgame with only isolated single matches left, leave an odd number of heaps containing one match.
4. Force your opponent into 1-1, 2-2, or 1-2-3 symmetrical positions.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is the difference between normal play and misère play in Nim?**
  A: In this misère version, the player forced to pick up the very last matchstick loses the game.
- **Q: Can you take matchsticks from multiple heaps in one turn?**
  A: No, standard Nim rules state you may take as many matches as you wish, but only from one single heap per turn.
- **Q: How many heaps are used in Game of Nim?**
  A: Standard matches feature three heaps containing 3, 5, and 7 matchsticks respectively.

---

### 52. Mini Reversi 6x6

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/strategy-reversi-mini/
- **Category**: Strategy & Tactics (https://wanjaaro.com/strategy-tactics/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Outflank opposing discs between your own to flip them over, finishing the match with majority board control.
- **What It Measures**: This board game measures boundary stability evaluation and positional sacrifice strategy. It evaluates your control of stable corner anchors versus temporary disc counts.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Place your disc on an empty square such that you trap one or more opponent discs between your new piece and another of your pieces. All trapped discs flip to your color.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Capture corner squares at all costs; corner discs can never be flipped over by your opponent.
2. Avoid playing adjacent to open corners (the "C-squares" and "X-squares") unless you are certain to capture the corner next turn.
3. Minimize early disc flips; having fewer discs in the mid-game leaves your opponent with fewer legal move options.
4. Control stable edges that connect directly into secured corners.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What grid size is used in Mini Reversi?**
  A: This compact version uses a 6x6 grid (36 squares) for faster, high-intensity tactical rounds.
- **Q: What happens if a player has no legal moves?**
  A: If you have no moves that outflank at least one opposing disc, your turn passes automatically to your opponent.
- **Q: How does the game end in Mini Reversi?**
  A: The game concludes when all 36 squares are filled or when neither player can make a legal move.

### 55. Hex Territory Conquer

- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **moves** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Connect your two opposite board edges with an unbroken chain of adjacent colored hexagonal tiles.
- **What It Measures**: This connection game measures topology connectivity planning and path blocking. It benchmarks your construction of un-blockable virtual connections and bridge templates.
- **How to Play & Rules**: You start at the top-left hex. Choose one of 5 colors. All adjacent hexes of that color are absorbed into your growing territory. Conquer more than 50% of the board before moves expire.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Use two-space "bridge" configurations; if your opponent enters one open gap, you immediately take the other.
2. Balance offensive path progression with defensive blocking moves across opposing diagonal corridors.
3. Control central hexagonal tiles early to maximize your branching route choices.
4. Remember that draws are mathematically impossible in Hex; one player must always form a connection.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Can a match of Hex ever end in a draw?**
  A: No, John Nash mathematically proved that the game of Hex can never end in a draw; one player will always complete a path.
- **Q: Which edges belong to which player?**
  A: Player one connects North to South with gold tiles, while player two connects West to East with blue tiles.
- **Q: What is a "bridge" in Hex strategy?**
  A: A bridge consists of two stones separated by two shared empty hexes, guaranteeing connection because the opponent cannot block both.

- **What It Measures**: This game measures auditory-motor tempo synchronization and millisecond rhythmic pacing. It records your timing delta relative to steady metronome beats.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A metronome beats at 120 BPM. Tap along in rhythm with the beat. Your score is based on how many milliseconds off-beat each tap lands (aim for ±15ms accuracy!).

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Internalize the tempo by nodding or tapping your foot slightly ahead of the first hit.
2. Tap to the audio click rather than relying solely on visual marker position.
3. Maintain a consistent down-stroke speed rather than hesitating as the beat arrives.
4. Avoid drifting ahead of the beat (rushing) when tempo increases.

- **Q: How is timing precision measured in BPM Metronome Tap?**
  A: Taps within 25 milliseconds of the beat center earn "Perfect" ratings; taps within 50ms score "Good".
- **Q: Do tempos change mid-song?**
  A: Stages maintain steady BPM tempos ranging from slow 60 BPM ballads to energetic 140 BPM techno tracks.
- **Q: Can you use the spacebar to tap instead of a mouse click?**
  A: Yes, keyboard spacebar input is supported and recommended for stable tactile rhythm tapping.

- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)

- **What It Measures**: This drill measures bimanual phase alternation and reciprocal tapping cadence. It benchmarks your ability to maintain a rapid, balanced 180-degree phase shift between two hands.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Place one finger / mouse on the Left Dot and one on the Right Dot. Guide both through their respective security gates when both gates open simultaneously.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Think of your fingers as walking legs: left, right, left, right in an unbroken gait.
2. Tap with equal force on both sides to prevent one hand from dominating the cadence.
3. Keep your finger lifts low to minimize travel time between alternating strokes.
4. Focus on the metronome beat indicator to prevent tempo drift.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Can you use a keyboard for Twin Gate Crossing?**
  A: Yes, keyboard controls use the Z key for left gate and the M key for right gate.
- **Q: What is a phase error in this game?**
  A: A phase error occurs if both fingers tap simultaneously or if one finger taps twice in succession.
- **Q: How long does a standard speed trial last?**
  A: Standard sessions run for 20 seconds of continuous alternating tapping.

### 65. Schulte 1-to-25 Matrix

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/speed-click-25/
- **Category**: Speed & Accuracy (https://wanjaaro.com/speed-accuracy/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **sec** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Locate and click numbers 1 through 25 on the 5x5 matrix in strict ascending numerical order as fast as possible.
- **What It Measures**: This test measures broad visual search speed and numerical scan sequencing. It benchmarks your peripheral visual scanning efficiency across a structured numerical field.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A 5x5 grid containing numbers 1 to 25 scrambled randomly. Click number 1, then 2, then 3, all the way to 25. Used by cosmonauts and speed-readers to train peripheral vision.
- **Verified Benchmark**: Metric: 25-number ascending visual search duration | Population Average: 32s – 45s | Elite Tier (Top 1%): < 20s | Source: Schulte Table standardized visual search assessment protocol

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Keep your eyes fixed on the center square (number 13) and use peripheral vision to locate numbers.
2. Avoid moving your head or tracing your finger across the screen; move only your eyes and mouse.
3. As you click one number, begin searching for the subsequent number before your hand returns.
4. Notice where numbers in the next tier (like 6-10 while clicking 1-5) are located to prepare your route.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is a Schulte Table?**
  A: Developed by German psychiatrist Walter Schulte, it is a standard psychological test used to measure visual search velocity and attention distribution.
- **Q: What is considered a fast completion time for a 5x5 Schulte Table?**
  A: The average adult completes a 25-number grid in 32 to 45 seconds; speed readers and trained esports players finish in under 20 seconds.
- **Q: What happens if you click a number out of order?**
  A: The grid flashes red and refuses to advance until the correct next sequential number is clicked.

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/math-24-solver/

- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard

- **What It Measures**: This game measures arithmetic factor exploration and flexible algebraic manipulation. It tests your ability to spot factors of 24 (like 3×8, 4×6, 2×12, or 24/1) among arbitrary digit sets.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Four numbers are drawn (e.g. 3, 3, 8, 8). Combine them using basic arithmetic operations so the final result is 24 (e.g. 8 / (3 - 8/3) = 24). Tap numbers and signs in sequence.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Look for ways to form classic factors of 24: such as 3 and 8, or 4 and 6, or 2 and 12.
2. If you have a 3 and an 8, see if your remaining two cards can be combined to form 1 (e.g. 7 - 6 = 1).
3. Look for fractions that multiply out, such as 8 / (1 - 1/3) = 24 on advanced puzzles.
4. Try making numbers that subtract or add to 24 (such as 20 + 4, or 27 - 3).

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Must you use all four number cards in your equation?**
  A: Yes, standard 24-game rules require you to use each of the four dealt numbers exactly once.
- **Q: Are parentheses allowed to control order of operations?**
  A: Yes, interactive parenthesis buttons allow you to nest operations cleanly before evaluating.
- **Q: Is every dealt hand of four cards guaranteed to have a solution?**
  A: All puzzle sets in this game are pre-filtered and mathematically verified to possess at least one valid solution.

### 76. Prime Detective

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/math-prime-or-composite/
- **Category**: Math & Mental Calc (https://wanjaaro.com/math-calculation/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Classify flashed whole numbers as either Prime or Composite as quickly and accurately as possible.
- **What It Measures**: This math game measures divisibility rule application and number theory categorization. It tests your speed at checking small factor multiples (2, 3, 5, 7, 11).
- **How to Play & Rules**: A number between 2 and 150 appears. Hit PRIME if it has no divisors other than 1 and itself; hit COMPOSITE if it has factors. Win points for speed and accuracy.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Any even number greater than 2 is immediately composite.
2. Use the digit-sum rule for 3: if the sum of all digits is divisible by 3, the number is composite.
3. Any number ending in 5 or 0 (other than 5 itself) is composite.
4. Memorize tricky small primes under 100 like 53, 59, 61, 71, 73, 79, 83, 89, and 97.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Is the number 1 considered a prime number?**
  A: No, in mathematics 1 is neither prime nor composite; it has only one positive divisor.
- **Q: Is the number 2 a prime number?**
  A: Yes, 2 is the smallest prime number and the only even prime number in existence.
- **Q: What is the highest number tested in Prime Detective?**
  A: Standard mode tests numbers up to 150, with master stages testing three-digit numbers up to 500.

### 81. Mental Rotation Challenge

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/visual-shape-rotate/
- **Category**: Visual & Geometry (https://wanjaaro.com/visual-geometry/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Determine whether a rotated 3D polygon is an exact rotation or a mirrored reflection of the target shape.
- **What It Measures**: This test measures mental rotation capability and 3D spatial transformation speed. It benchmarks how accurately you mentally manipulate three-dimensional objects in space.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Two isometric shapes are shown at different angular orientations. Decide if they are the exact same shape merely rotated in 3D space, or if they are inverted chiral mirror images.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Pick one distinct protruding feature or colored face and mentally track where it would land after rotation.
2. Check the handedness of corners: if a point turns clockwise on the original, it must remain clockwise on a true rotation.
3. Use keyboard shortcut keys (Left for "Mirrored", Right for "Rotated") for fastest response times.
4. Do not try to rotate the entire object at once; focus on two connected perpendicular edges.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What is mental rotation in spatial cognitive psychology?**
  A: First quantified by Shepard and Metzler in 1971, mental rotation describes the internal process of rotating 2D or 3D mental representations.
- **Q: What rotation angles are tested in this challenge?**
  A: Angles range from 45° to 315° across all three rotational axes (yaw, pitch, and roll).
- **Q: How does response time correlate with rotation angle?**
  A: Response latency typically increases linearly with the degrees of rotation needed to align the shapes.

- **Category**: Visual & Geometry (https://wanjaaro.com/visual-geometry/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **sec** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Complete the missing half of a symmetrical pixel art grid across a central vertical or horizontal mirror axis.
- **What It Measures**: This game measures bilateral symmetry perception and coordinate mirror reflection. It tests your accuracy in translating coordinates across a reflection axis.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A vertical mirror line divides the canvas. Replicate the illuminated tiles on the right side so the image displays bilateral symmetry. Complete in minimum seconds.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Count outward from the center mirror line rather than counting inward from the outer wall.
2. Paint pixel blocks in symmetrical pairs: one unit left of center maps to one unit right of center.
3. Look at overall silhouette outlines before filling internal decorative pixel squares.
4. Use drag-to-paint to fill continuous symmetrical lines swiftly.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Can the mirror axis be horizontal as well as vertical?**
  A: Yes, early stages use vertical reflection axes, while advanced levels introduce horizontal and diagonal mirror axes.
- **Q: What grid sizes are used in Symmetry Mirror Painter?**
  A: Grids scale from 8x8 pixels on casual puzzles up to 16x16 pixels on complex tapestries.
- **Q: How is painting accuracy scored?**
  A: Scores reflect the percentage of correctly placed mirror pixels minus deductions for misplaced blocks.

### 83. Planar Graph Untangler

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/visual-tangled-lines/
- **Category**: Visual & Geometry (https://wanjaaro.com/visual-geometry/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **moves** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Drag vertex nodes across the canvas until no two connecting line segments cross or intersect each other.
- **What It Measures**: This puzzle measures planar graph untangling and topology visualization. It evaluates your spatial reorganization of intersecting nodes into non-overlapping planar embeddings.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A graph of interconnected vertices begins in a tangled knot with crossing red lines. Drag the nodes until every line turns blue and no two lines intersect. A pure topology puzzle.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Move nodes with the highest number of connecting edges toward the outside perimeter of the circle.
2. Place nodes with few connections near the center where they are less likely to cross paths.
3. Look for triangles or loops of three nodes and spread their corners wide apart.
4. Work on resolving one intersecting line crossover at a time rather than shifting everything at once.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Is every graph in Planar Graph Untangler guaranteed to be solvable?**
  A: Yes, all generated graphs are mathematically planar, meaning they can always be untangled with zero line crossings.
- **Q: How do you know when a line is untangled?**
  A: Intersecting lines glow bright red, while fully cleared non-intersecting lines turn solid emerald green.
- **Q: What is the Kuratowski theorem related to planar graphs?**
  A: Kuratowski's theorem states that a finite graph is planar if and only if it does not contain subdivisions of K5 or K3,3 utility graphs.

2. Mentally unfold line segments into straight lines to compare total length.

### 88. Mirror Coordinate Plotter

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/visual-mirror-reflection/
- **Category**: Visual & Geometry (https://wanjaaro.com/visual-geometry/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Plot the exact Cartesian coordinates of a point after reflecting it across a diagonal or cardinal mirror line.
- **What It Measures**: This spatial drill measures Cartesian coordinate transformation and reflection geometry. It tests your calculation of mirrored coordinate pairs (x, y) across varying reflection axes.
- **How to Play & Rules**: A point is marked on a coordinate grid alongside a diagonal mirror line (y = x). Tap the exact grid coordinate where the point will appear after reflection across the mirror.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. When reflecting over the vertical y-axis, invert the sign of the x-coordinate: (x, y) becomes (-x, y).
2. When reflecting over the horizontal x-axis, invert the sign of the y-coordinate: (x, y) becomes (x, -y).
3. When reflecting over the diagonal line y = x, swap the coordinates completely: (x, y) becomes (y, x).
4. Measure the perpendicular distance from the point to the mirror line; the reflection lies at the exact same distance on the opposite side.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What coordinate axes are featured in Mirror Coordinate Plotter?**
  A: Problems feature standard Cartesian grids with reflections across x=0, y=0, y=x, and offset parallel lines.
- **Q: How do you submit your answer?**
  A: Click directly on the destination grid intersection point, or type the coordinates into the input box.
- **Q: What happens if you click one grid unit off?**
  A: The system highlights your offset error in red and displays the correct mathematical reflection line.

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/casual-golf-putt/
- **Category**: Casual & Arcade (https://wanjaaro.com/casual-arcade/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **moves** (lower values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Modulate stroke angle and power to putt the golf ball across turf slopes and into the cup in the fewest strokes.
- **What It Measures**: This sports physics game measures kinetic force modulation and surface slope trajectory estimation. It tests your judgment of ball friction, bank angles, and cup capture speed.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Drag backward from the golf ball to aim and set stroke power. Release to putt the ball across the green, around sand traps and obstacles, directly into the flag cup in least strokes.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Pull back gently on short putts; hitting the cup with excessive speed will cause the ball to lip out.
2. Read green contour arrows: aim uphill of the hole to allow natural slope break to steer the ball toward the cup.
3. Use wooden boundary walls to bank shots around sand traps and water hazards.
4. Avoid sand bunkers, as landing in sand dramatically deadens ball roll and adds penalty strokes.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: How do you aim and set stroke power in Mini Golf Hole-in-One?**
  A: Drag backward from the golf ball to draw an aiming arrow; pulling farther back increases stroke velocity.
- **Q: What is par for each hole in Mini Golf?**
  A: Standard holes have a par rating between 2 and 4 strokes, with hole-in-one aces awarding massive bonus points.
- **Q: Can you putt backwards if you get stuck behind an obstacle?**
  A: Yes, you can aim 360 degrees in any direction to bounce off boundary walls and escape tricky corners.

### 101. Klondike Solitaire Classic

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/solitaire/
- **Category**: Casual & Arcade (https://wanjaaro.com/casual-arcade/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Sort all 52 cards into the four foundation piles by suit from Ace to King, building alternating color tableau runs.
- **What It Measures**: This classic card game measures depth-first sequencing strategy and probabilistic card excavation. It benchmarks your card ordering decisions and tableau column management.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Build the 4 foundation piles from Ace to King by suit. In the tableau, build descending sequences in alternating colors. Drag or click cards to move them.
- **Verified Benchmark**: Metric: Moves and deal win probability | Population Average: 110 – 145 moves (~33% win rate on standard deal) | Elite Tier (Top 1%): < 85 moves (> 80% win rate on solvable draws) | Source: Wolter, Y. (2007) Klondike Solitaire probability analysis, Stanford University / Mathematica

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Always prioritize moves that uncover face-down cards in deep tableau columns over drawing from the stock deck.
2. Keep empty columns open specifically for Kings to unlock long buried card stacks.
3. Do not rush to transfer cards into foundation piles if they might still be needed to hold tableau sequences.
4. Examine both red and black placement options before committing cards to tableau columns.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What percentage of Klondike Solitaire deals are theoretically winnable?**
  A: Mathematical analysis by Stanford researchers (Wolter, 2007) shows that approximately 82% of Klondike deals are solvable with optimal play, though everyday win rates average 33%.
- **Q: Does this version use Draw 1 or Draw 3 rules?**
  A: Standard casual mode uses Draw 1 for a smooth, solvable experience, with an optional Draw 3 mode available in settings.
- **Q: What tools are provided on the solitaire board?**
  A: The game features unlimited undo, auto-complete for cleared tableaus, hints, and local score tracking.

### 102. Master Sudoku 9x9

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/sudoku/
- **Category**: Logic & Puzzles (https://wanjaaro.com/logic-puzzles/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Fill the 9x9 grid so every row, column, and 3x3 subgrid contains digits 1 through 9 with zero repeats.
- **What It Measures**: This number puzzle measures deductive constraint satisfaction and logical candidate elimination. It benchmarks systematic elimination reasoning without guessing.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Fill the 9x9 grid so every row, column, and 3x3 block contains the digits 1 through 9 exactly once without repeating.
- **Verified Benchmark**: Metric: Single-digit deduction completion time | Population Average: 12 – 18 minutes (Standard 9x9) | Elite Tier (Top 1%): < 5 minutes | Source: World Puzzle Federation (WPF) World Sudoku Championship scoring standard for medium 9x9 grids

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Scan for "naked singles"—cells where eight other digits are already present in that row, column, or 3x3 block.
2. Use pencil candidate notes in cells that have only two or three possibilities.
3. Look for "hidden singles"—a digit that only has one legal location remaining inside an entire 3x3 box.
4. Identify "naked pairs" sharing identical candidates in a line to eliminate those numbers from neighboring cells.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: Do you ever need to guess to solve a Sudoku puzzle on Wanjaaro?**
  A: No, every puzzle on Wanjaaro is handcrafted to possess a unique solution reachable through pure logical deduction.
- **Q: What is the benchmark time for solving a medium 9x9 Sudoku grid?**
  A: Recreational solvers typically complete a standard grid in 12 to 18 minutes; competitive tournament solvers finish in under 5 minutes.
- **Q: What tools are built into the game board?**
  A: The board includes pencil note mode, conflict highlighting, undo/redo history, and digit completion indicators.

### 103. Mahjong Solitaire Classic

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/mahjong/
- **Category**: Casual & Arcade (https://wanjaaro.com/casual-arcade/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Match and clear open pairs of identical traditional Chinese tiles until the entire layered pyramid board is cleared.
- **What It Measures**: This tile-matching puzzle measures multi-layer visual depth analysis and peripheral edge unblocking. It tests how you prioritize freeing trapped tiles across complex 3D layouts.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Select and match pairs of identical free tiles to clear the board. A tile is free if it has no tiles above it and has at least one open side (left or right).

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Focus on clearing tall vertical stacks and long horizontal rows first, as they trap the highest number of hidden tiles.
2. Never match a pair immediately if doing so leaves other critical rows blocked; survey all candidate matches.
3. Remember that Season tiles match with any Season, and Flower tiles match with any Flower.
4. Keep track of tile quadruplets: if three matching tiles are visible, matching two of them frees the remaining one.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What makes a tile "free" to match in Mahjong Solitaire?**
  A: A tile is free if: 1) No other tile rests directly on top of it, and 2) Either its left edge or right edge is completely open with no touching neighbor.
- **Q: How many total tiles are in a classic Mahjong Solitaire set?**
  A: A standard game features 144 tiles: three suits (Dots, Bamboos, Characters) from 1 to 9, four Winds, three Dragons, four Seasons, and four Flowers.
- **Q: Is every starting Mahjong layout guaranteed solvable?**
  A: Yes, boards generated on Wanjaaro use a reverse-deconstruction algorithm that guarantees every layout has a solvable matching sequence.

### 104. Picross Nonogram Logic

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/nonogram/
- **Category**: Logic & Puzzles (https://wanjaaro.com/logic-puzzles/)
- **Difficulty**: Hard
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Use row and column numerical run clues to deduce which cells to fill and which to cross out, revealing a pixel illustration.
- **What It Measures**: This Japanese picture puzzle measures cross-referencing logic and binary grid deduction. It evaluates how you intersect row and column line run constraints.
- **How to Play & Rules**: The numbers along rows and columns indicate groups of consecutive filled squares. Left-click or tap to fill a square; right-click or toggle cross mode to mark empty cells.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Begin by solving rows or columns where the clue sum plus intervening spaces equals the full grid length.
2. Use overlap logic: when a single run is greater than half the line length, the middle squares must always be filled.
3. Always mark guaranteed empty cells with an X to prevent accidental fills and narrow down remaining options.
4. Cross-check row markings against column clues immediately after filling any square.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: What does a clue of "3 2" mean in a Nonogram puzzle?**
  A: It indicates a run of 3 consecutive filled cells, followed by at least one empty space, followed by a run of 2 filled cells.
- **Q: Can you make mistakes without losing the game?**
  A: Mistake checking mode gives you up to three penalty strikes for incorrectly filled squares before round end.
- **Q: What sizes of picture grids are available?**
  A: Puzzles start with beginner 5x5 grids and expand up to detailed 15x15 pixel art pictures.

### 105. Daily Mind Puzzle

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/daily-puzzle/
- **Category**: Logic & Puzzles (https://wanjaaro.com/logic-puzzles/)
- **Difficulty**: Easy
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **pts** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Group 16 related words into four secret thematic quartets within four allowable mistake lives.
- **What It Measures**: This daily challenge measures semantic categorization and associative reasoning. It benchmarks your ability to identify shared conceptual themes while resisting deceptive overlap traps.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Find four groups of four related items that share an underlying concept or category. You have 4 mistake lives to solve the daily puzzle.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Watch out for words that seem to fit into two distinct categories; find unambiguous groups first.
2. Check for wordplay themes like compound words, homophones, rhymes, or missing prefixes.
3. Do not guess randomly; if you are unsure, look for an anchor word that can only belong to one domain.
4. Submit groups in order of confidence to preserve your four mistake lives for tricky remaining words.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: When does the Daily Mind Puzzle reset with a new board?**
  A: A new handcrafted 16-word board unlocks every single midnight based on your local device calendar date.
- **Q: Can you share your daily result with friends?**
  A: Yes, after solving or completing the board, you can copy formatted emoji color tiles to share your solve streak.
- **Q: How are the four secret categories color-coded?**
  A: Categories range in difficulty from yellow (straightforward) and green, to blue, and purple (tricky wordplay or trivia).

### 106. Galactic Ore Miner (Idle)

- **Canonical URL**: https://wanjaaro.com/idle-games/
- **Category**: Casual & Arcade (https://wanjaaro.com/casual-arcade/)
- **Difficulty**: Medium
- **Controls**: Mouse, Touch, and Keyboard
- **Scoring**: Measured in **ore** (higher values indicate superior performance)
- **Objective**: Excavate cosmic minerals, purchase automated plasma drill rigs, and ascend through prestige tiers for permanent multipliers.
- **What It Measures**: This incremental game measures exponential resource compounding and investment efficiency planning. It benchmarks how effectively you balance active clicking against passive production upgrades.
- **How to Play & Rules**: Click the cosmic core to extract ore, purchase automated plasma drills and orbital extractors, upgrade click efficiency, and ascend for permanent cosmic multipliers.

**Gameplay & Strategy Tips**:
1. Invest early mining profits into automated plasma extractors to build sustainable passive ore per second (OPS).
2. Purchase production multiplier upgrades whenever they cost less than 15 minutes of current passive output.
3. Save your ascension prestige reset for when your current mineral income slows to a crawl.
4. Prioritize permanent cosmic prestige perks that boost base extractor output across all future runs.

**Frequently Asked Questions**:
- **Q: How does the Ascension prestige mechanic work in Galactic Ore Miner?**
  A: Ascending resets your current unspent ore and drill equipment in exchange for permanent cosmic shards that multiply all future ore extraction rates.
- **Q: Does the game continue mining minerals while closed?**
  A: Yes, passive offline progress calculates earned minerals based on your last recorded timestamp upon reopening.
- **Q: Where is your idle mining progress saved?**
  A: All equipment levels, cosmic shards, total extracted ore, and prestige multipliers are stored in your browser's localStorage.
